Worst experience ever.

There was an issue with my mother’s name about 10 years ago which had already been resolved and the passport was issued. However, during her recent passport renewal, we were told that the issue is still not cleared digitally. Because of this, she was asked to travel all the way from Nashik to the Bandra passport office — which feels completely unreasonable and poorly managed.

She reached there after 12 pm due to delayed trains, and despite having already travelled such a long distance, she was not allowed entry as they do not accept visitors after 12 pm. This lack of flexibility shows a complete disconnect from ground realities.

On top of that, we noticed clear preferential treatment — some politically connected individuals with police escort were allowed inside without any issues, while ordinary citizens were turned away.

To make things worse, there are no proper basic facilities like drinking water or toilets near the office. In extreme heat of around 33°C, my mother was even refused drinking water when she requested it.

It is disappointing that from common citizens to those in power, there seems to be a lack of basic empathy, accountability, and consideration for people’s time and hardship. The entire system feels rigid, unfair, and insensitive to the public it is meant to serve.

Google need to put zero star an option.

Pathetic Service – No Accountability for Clerical Errors
I am beyond disappointed with the service at RPO Mumbai (BKC). My son was issued a passport with a clerical error (Mother’s name) despite us providing the official Gazette document during the appointment. Instead of owning up to their mistake, the staff is extremely rude and unprofessional.
When I approached them for a correction, I was given two choices:
Wait indefinitely for an internal "investigation" between offices.
Pay the full fee again for a "reissue" to expedite their own mistake.
To save time, I agreed to pay, but the incompetence didn't stop there. Counter staff are consistently late. Today, the officer arrived at 2:25 PM for a 2:00 PM shift. When I asked the adjacent counter why there was a delay, I was told, "Ask him yourself when he arrives."
The lack of accountability is shocking. They make the mistake, treat the citizens like they are doing them a favor, and then force you to pay again for their errors. If you are going here, be prepared for zero help and high levels of arrogance.
